title: FTSE Russell — preliminary June 2027 additions/deletions published (five weeks before implementation)
source: EST: rule-derived from the index owner's ground rules, with the arithmetic convention confirmed against both published instances. FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026 (lseg.com dam PDF, HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, text-extracted in-session 2026-09-06), Appendix F's schedule table gives, for the June semi-annual reconstitution, Preliminary Information Released = "Five weeks prior to implementation", Query Period = "For two weeks following preliminary announcement", Lock down = "Three weeks after query period ends", Implementation = "4th Friday of June". Section 4.3.1's IPO paragraph repeats it: June changes "are announced five weeks prior to implementation". The schedule is internally consistent -- 5 weeks prelim = 2 weeks query + 3 weeks lockdown -- which is itself a check on the reading. June 2027's implementation is Friday 2027-06-25 (see russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25.json for the two-clause derivation and the 36-of-36-year proof that the section 9.3.1 carve-out never changes it), so five weeks prior is Friday 2027-05-21, and the query period ends Friday 2027-06-04. THE FIVE-WEEK CONVENTION IS NOT ASSUMED -- it is confirmed against both instances the owner has actually published, read off lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution the same session (HTTP 200, 228,333 bytes): June 2026 implemented 2026-06-26 "following the publication of preliminary lists beginning on May 22", exactly 35 days = 5 weeks; and December 2026, whose Appendix F rule is four weeks, publishes 2026-11-13 for a 2026-12-11 implementation, exactly 28 days = 4 weeks. Two conventions, two published instances, both exact to the day. Filed estimate because no FTSE Russell 2027 reconstitution calendar exists yet -- the ground rules state one "is published each spring", so the 2027 calendar is not due until spring 2027; this is an unpublished document, not a blocked fetch. Promote on a published FTSE Russell 2027 recon calendar naming the preliminary date. Discovered during the russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 initial research (2026-09-06). WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ENTRY FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION DATE: 2027-06-25 is when the trade happens; 2027-05-21 is when the information arrives. The preliminary additions/deletions list is the canonical information event in the published index-effect literature -- from the announcement the membership changes are public and the flow is forecastable, and the five weeks between announcement and implementation are the window that literature studies. A calendar that tracks only the execution date cannot see the announcement, which is the half of the mechanic that is actually an information event. THE PROPOSER IS EXPLICIT THAT ITS OWN MEASUREMENTS DO NOT MAKE THIS ACTIONABLE, and files it as coverage rather than as a signal: the D-5 -> D0 run-up into implementation measured +0.62% IWM-vs-SPY against -0.06% unconditional (one-sided bootstrap p=8.1%, n=11) and the D0 -> D+5 reversal -0.87% (p=4.8%), but the twelve-month placebo puts one month under p=0.05 by chance alone and window length swings p from 1.7% to 24.4% -- a registered hypothesis, not an edge. The announcement window itself (2027-05-21 -> 2027-06-25) was NOT measured by this session at all; no claim is made about it, and that gap is the honest reason to have the date on the calendar before anyone needs it. Impact low, status estimate: an announcement moves no shares, the effect is unmeasured here, no house playbook is index-flow-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-06, zero hits), and shorting is blocked house-wide -- so it widens caution and licenses nothing. Kind `sector` matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
